headline: Brazil ties data-center tax relief to clean power, local capacity and R&D commitments
summary: Brazil's Lei 15.504/2026 creates Redata, a five-year tax-incentive regime for qualifying data-center installation, modernization and expansion, including AI training and inference. Applicants must make at least 10% of the effective processing, storage and data-treatment supply installed with Redata benefits available to Brazil's domestic market; the law calculates that commitment using domestic gross revenue as a share of total gross revenue from the benefited services, with implementation details left to regulation. Applicants must also meet renewable or low-emission electricity and sustainability requirements, keep cooling WUE at or below 0.05 L/kWh, and invest 2% of incentivized ICT-product purchases in local digital-economy R&D. The law suspends specified taxes on eligible ICT equipment; PIS/Pasep, Cofins and IPI provisions currently run through 2026-12-31 under the tax-transition clause.
